title: Ostrich Walk with Bix and the Oldsmobile arrangement
summary: He and Bix worked up Ostrich Walk at Goldkette's school, and he wrote In My Merry Oldsmobile for a car company party.

story.theme_name: Writing and arranging: how musicians compose
story.community_name: Writing, arranging and composing: how the music gets made

blocks.x: Well, they let me go but who to follow, what to do. In other words, where am I going? What am I supposed to do? So I remember Bix and I got together one night and went over to the Goldkette school. Goldkette had a school there, a music school and he had rooms there and we were told that Russ Morgan taught over there a couple of times or taught some things over there; but they had nice grand pianos in there; and we went over there one night after the

job and Bix, you know, he had the interest, he said, 'What do you say we get together and do something?' Oh, fine, I'd love to do something. Well, he said, 'let's do Ostrich Walk,' go over there and sit down and he plays a little bit and I said, 'Okay, I don't even know the tune, how does it go.' So he sits down and plays it and he plays a little introduction, plays the thing over. So we got started on it, you know how it is, you get together and one thing leads to another. 'All right, put this down, let me get that down.' And he plays around some more and let me get this down, let me get that down, and then we get a melody down, so we got a chorus down and we got another chorus and we worked out a saxophone chorus and an ensemble and a couple of things and the first thing you know, we had an arrangement. We were there quite a bit. Took it over a couple of days, and they liked that. Now, this would have been a plan if we had gone on to more Dixieland, but there was just that spotty thing, 'let's do this, let's do that,' and then they come up with a couple other tunes that they had to have, like Jean came around one time and said, 'The Oldsmobile people want me to do -- we're going to play at a party out there and they want a couple of arrangements made, one in waltz and one in fox trot, In My Merry Oldsmobile.' Well, don't you know, I guess they said, 'They'll record it.' So we made it and I had nothing

to do with the vocal. I had made it all instrumental. Well, you know, the guys got together and made a quartet out of it and later on when they went there and they made a record of it, made a record both sides. One side fox trot and the other side waltz and you know, Bix takes off in one of those places. It's a collector's item, guys want to get a record of "My Merry Oldsmobile."
